newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sells 4.703 bln reais in Treasury papers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sells 4.703 bln reais in Treasury papers.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank, on behalf of the National Treasury, raised 4.703 billion reais in an auction of notes and letters, dealers said.
A total of 2.933 billion reais was sold in two series of National Treasury Letters known as LTNs.

A total of 1.541 billon reais of 184-day LTNs, due in Feb 1 1998, was sold at an overnight call money rate of 2.286 percent a month. The Central Bank also sold 1.392 billion reais of 365-day, due in Aug 1, 1998, at a call money rate of 2.379 percent a month.
A total of 734 million reais was sold in two series of dollar-indexed National Treasury notes (NTN-D).

The bank sold 373 million reais of NTN-D notes, which are due on Aug 1, 1999, and pay an annual yield of 9.99 percent. The bank also sold 361 million reais of NTN-D notes coming due Aug 1, 2000, paying an annual yield of 10 percent.

Some 1.036 billion reais were sold in National Treasury notes (NTN-H) indexed to the variation of Brazil's reference rate (TR). The notes, which are due Feb 1, 1998, pay annual yields of 12.54 percent plus the variation of the TR in the maturity period.
